reforms.description: The federal government has implemented a flexible funding system for First Nations communities, allowing for ten-year grants instead of annual appropriations, which reduces administrative burdens and provides greater discretion in resource allocation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Providing more predictable funding can enhance the capacity of First Nations communities to engage in long-term planning and development.
reforms.status_evidence: The funding system has been implemented and is currently in operation.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform is significant for First Nations but does not represent a system-wide change.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government funds First Nations communities with various flexible funding instruments... began to offer ten-year grants, which afford their governments a lower administrative and reporting burden.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The flexible funding system for First Nations communities includes ten-year grants, which can support R&D activities and reduce administrative burdens.
